source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Continue lisinopril until the second trimester because fetal toxicity is not a concern early in pregnancy.","B":"Notify the prescriber promptly because lisinopril should be stopped as soon as pregnancy is detected.","C":"Reduce the lisinopril dose and continue it because lower exposure removes the fetal toxicity risk.","D":"Continue lisinopril if blood pressure is controlled because stable pressure prevents fetal toxicity."}}
source_row.rationale: Lisinopril carries a boxed warning for fetal toxicity and should be discontinued as soon as pregnancy is detected. Option B is correct. Dose reduction or adequate blood-pressure control does not remove the fetal risk, and waiting until the second trimester is inconsistent with the label.
source_row.source_detail: Boxed Warning/Fetal Toxicity and Warnings and Precautions §5.1: when pregnancy is detected, discontinue lisinopril as soon as possible; renin-angiotensin system drugs can cause fetal injury or death. DailyMed label updated 2026-07-03; currentness live-rechecked 2026-08-15. source_row.stem: A client taking lisinopril reports a newly confirmed pregnancy. Which nursing action is most appropriate?
